head.title: What's New in the XSLT/XPath Extension for VS Code

meta.name: description
meta.content: What's new in the XSLT/XPath extension for VS Code: the features of releases 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2, from the debugger and XSpec to Schematron and profiling.

div.p: Highlights of the features added in releases 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2:

ul.li: Schematron - For editing, Schematron files are checked as SchXslt2, the processor XSpec uses. There are quick fixes for any XSLT instructions that SchXslt2 ignores or doesn't run. Auto-completion follows ISO Schematron 2025. Schematron: Validate validates an XML file with a schema, with failed assertions shown in the Problems view. Messages in Schematron can use text value templates - a non-standard extension, with a setting - and Schematron: Export Standard Copy... writes a standardised copy that will run on standard processors. Debug a schema with breakpoints and stepping on its rules, lets and assertions, in the phase shown in the status bar

Profiler - profile any XSLT with Saxon-PE/EE to see a breakdown on performance: the time of each template, function and global variable, the slowest first, with times above the declarations in the editor, warm-up runs left out, and earlier profiles appear in the Timeline view for comparison. A Schematron schema is profiled the same way, with the time of each rule
XSpec test times - with Saxon-PE/EE, the Test Explorer shows how long each test took, and an XSpec file's Timeline shows how long its tests took on each run

Mapping from source XML to the XSLT templates that processed them. After a debug session, hover over an element in the input file to see the template rules - and xsl:for-each, xsl:for-each-group and xsl:iterate instructions - that processed it, its attributes and its text - or the Schematron rules that fired for it - and go to them; above each template or instruction, the nodes it processed. From the output view, go to the input that part of the output was written for, as well as to the instruction that wrote it

AI assistants that run your stylesheets (MCP, experimental) - the new run_configuration tool gives an assistant the exact Saxon command Quick Run would use for a stylesheet - your Saxon jar, XML context file, parameters, catalog and workspace packages - so what it runs gives the same result as yours. Each VS Code window now has its own server, so an assistant in a project's folder uses that project's window

Checking files that aren't open - Check Problems in Workspace and Check Problems in Folder lint stylesheets without opening them, and Check Modules Using Package (also a CodeLens on xsl:package) checks the modules that use a package, for when a change to its visibility breaks them. A private package component is now reported as private where it's used, with a quick fix to make it public

Step-through debugging - debug stylesheets with SaxonJ (any edition, including Saxon-HE): breakpoints with conditions, hit counts and logpoints, stepping through templates, functions and multi-line XPath expressions - including inline functions - and the variables, context item and output so far, as you go

XSpec tests - run and debug XSpec tests from the Test Explorer, for stylesheets and Schematron, with each failure's expected and actual results side by side, and breakpoints in the stylesheet or the XSpec file. XSpec files are checked as you edit them, against XSpec's schema and the stylesheet they test, with auto-completion, hover help and navigation between the tests and the stylesheet. XSpec 4.1.2 is included

XSLT packages - Workspace packages are automatically discovered from their xsl:package name and version and supplied to Saxon when running or debugging stylesheets. Component visibility, xsl:expose, and xsl:accept are handled exactly as Saxon does. Issues with xsl:accept, xsl:override, and package modes are flagged while you edit, with quick fixes available.

Find Nodes with XPath - run XPath expressions on an XML file from a query file below it, with the XPath editor's checks and auto-completion: the nodes found are listed to step through, and values are shown after each expression. Replaces Goto XPath

MCP server for AI assistants (experimental) - tools an assistant such as Claude Code or GitHub Copilot can call to check stylesheets that aren't open, find declarations and references, show a module's imports, and describe item types and built-in functions

Tracing values with xdm:trace() - trace a value anywhere within an XPath expression: like trace(), it returns the value unchanged, but writes it formatted as xdm:debug() does. Wrap with xdm:trace() adds it around a selected expression, and Remove xdm:trace() - keep the expression removes the call and its other arguments, leaving just the expression

Converting a library to a package - Analyse as Package... reports what would have to change for a library that stylesheets import to become a package, and Convert to Package... makes the changes across the workspace - the library's visibility, the stylesheets' overrides, even a shared unnamed mode - shown in the Refactor Preview before they're made

Full language support for XSLT 4.0 in Saxon 13 - type-aware auto-completion, checks, hover help and refactoring for the XSLT 4.0 and XPath 4.0 features Saxon 13 implements: new syntax and item types, keyword arguments and optional parameters, xsl:switch, and documentation notes with xsl:note

Code Documentation - documentation within xsl:note elements provides hover assistance using tags based on xqdoc along with Markdown descriptions. In an XSLT 3.0 stylesheet, xsl:note needs Saxon PE/EE 12.8 or later and the XSLT.validation.xslt30ItemTypesAndNotes setting.
Records and Enums - auto-completion, checks, hover help and refactoring for XPath 4.0 record and enumeration types, from map constructors to xsl:switch cases
JSON and JNodes - XPath 4.0 path expressions on JSON, with auto-completion, checks and hover help for steps on JNodes with a record type, and JNode paths shown by xdm:debug()
Quick Run - run the active stylesheet with a shortcut or the toolbar button, without configuring a task first - with SaxonJ, SaxonJS or the new SaxonC support
Inferred imports - the top-level stylesheet of a module is found from the workspace, without opening it first, and the new XSLT Imports view shows its tree of imports and includes
XML Catalogs - resolve the href of xsl:import and xsl:include, e.g. the http: URI of a shared library, to a local file with an OASIS XML catalog - also passed to Saxon when a stylesheet is run
Editing - signature help and richer hover help for functions and templates, more auto-completion, and the new Wrap with... refactoring
Print debugging - one auto-completed xsl:message for all the in-scope variables, formatted and colored with xdm:debug()
